subject: Budget range validation — Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Great chat — next steps on budget & token volumes

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple of follow-ups so we can size the right pilot and procurement path: 

Summary notes from call:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + automated post-chat summarization for fraud review.
- Expected Q2 pilot: integrate Redwood API for generation + embeddings for semantic search.
- API integration timeline: 2-4 weeks for initial integration, subset of flows live within a month.

Cost/volume details we discussed (please confirm):
- Per-user per-day conversational average: ~450 tokens generated + 175 tokens input (total ~625 tokens)
- Active users for pilot: 250-500 MAU (monthly active)
- Expected request concurrency: spiky (peak support hours) — want to understand both average and 95th pct.

Pricing/qualification asks for procurement:
1) Can you confirm an expected monthly token volume band? (e.g., 100M-500M / 500M-1B / 1B+)
2) Do you have a target unit economics we should be aware of (target $ per 1M tokens or target monthly spend)?
3) Any procurement thresholds or approval limits we should plan around (e.g., >$50k requires exec sign-off, legal review timelines)?

Suggested next steps:
- If you can reply with the monthly token band + procurement threshold, I'll put together a 3-tier pilot pricing and an MSA summary.
- Attached is our high-level pricing deck; I’ll also draft a mutual action plan if we have the budget band.

Attachment: redwood-pricing-deck.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

On Wed, 18 Feb 2026 at 15:10 Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — looks good. Talk soon.

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Li <anya.li@acmepay.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Great chat — next steps on budget & token volumes

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers from our side so you can size things: 

1) Monthly token band (estimated):
- Conservative pilot: ~120M tokens/month
- Mid pilot: ~320M tokens/month
- Scale projection (post-pilot, 6mo): 800M-1.2B tokens/month

2) Target unit economics / spend:
- Our procurement target for SaaS AI services is to stay under ~$900-1,200 per 1M tokens (net effective), depending on SLA and data controls.
- For pilot, finance has allocated a monthly budget band of $15k-45k (we can stretch to $60k with business case).

3) Procurement thresholds / approvals:
- Anya (cc'd) is procurement lead — anything > $50k/month will need VP procurement approval + legal SOW.
- Standard procurement timeline: 3-6 weeks once statement of work & pricing agreed.
- We require SOC 2 Type II + data processing addendum for any production contract.

We can proceed with a pilot scoped to the mid pilot (~320M tokens) to validate. If you can share a pricing view for the 120M vs 320M vs 800M bands (including pilot discounts and pre-paid reserved capacity options), that would help.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Product & Engineering | Acme Payments
samir.patel@acmepay.com | 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Anya Li <anya.li@acmepay.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Great chat — next steps on budget & token volumes

Great — this is super helpful, Samir. Confirming I got the bands and thresholds. A few clarifying notes and proposed next steps: 

Clarifications:
- We can support the SOC 2 + DPA requirements; I’ll loop in security for the pack.
- VP approval threshold noted (> $50k/month). For deals that cross that mark we typically coordinate an exec intro and a short procurement kickoff to speed review.

Pricing approach (initial thoughts):
- 120M tokens/mo (pilot-small): recommended on-hosted pricing with a pilot discount — target net ~$1,100 per 1M tokens -> ~$132k/mo (note: this is list-equivalent; we'll show net pilot pricing).
- 320M tokens/mo (pilot-mid): blended reserved pricing + pilot credits -> target net ~$950 per 1M tokens -> ~$304k/mo.
- 800M tokens/mo (scale projection): reserved capacity pricing -> target net ~$700 per 1M tokens -> ~$560k/mo.

These are rough targets — we can tighten once Dylan (cc'd) confirms ops/compute assumptions. For procurement, we can structure a month-to-month pilot with an agreed consumption cap to stay under $50k/mo if you want to avoid VP sign-off initially, or run a paid pilot at the mid band with a standing PO + SOW to speed rollout.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll draft a short mutual action plan (attached) with milestones and acceptance criteria for the pilot.
2) Dylan will prepare an ops-backed cost estimate showing how we get to the ~$950/$700 numbers (batching, KV caching assumptions, reserved capacity delta).
3) If you prefer, we can set a 30-min call next week with procurement + engineering to walk the proposal.

Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Let me know which pilot path you prefer (cap under $50k vs mid-band paid pilot). Happy to set the procurement call.

Best,
Marissa

---
On Thu, 19 Feb 2026 at 09:22 Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — catching up with Anya now.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Li <anya.li@acmepay.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Great chat — next steps on budget & token volumes

Hi Samir / Marissa — Dylan here (infra/solutions). Quick note on the ops-side sizing and unit economics that feed the pricing targets Marissa shared: 

- Assumptions I used: average seq len 625 tokens, 95th pct concurrency multiplier 1.8, KV cache hit ~22% for your support flows.
- With continuous batching and prefix caching we can hit an effective token cost that maps to the ~$950 per 1M tokens for the 320M band when using a 6-12 month reserved profile + modest pilot credits.
- For the under-$50k pilot option, we recommend a consumption cap + throttling policy and a short (4-6 week) pilot with agreed acceptance criteria so we avoid surprise overages.

I’ll follow up by EOD Friday with a short cost-breakdown spreadsheet (instance types, expected throughput, reserved vs burst) and a recommended config for the pilot.

If helpful, we can propose an internal playbook for procurement: PO -> SOW -> security review -> provisioned pilot (typical 3-5 week turn).

Thanks — happy to jump on the procurement call next week.

Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | (415) 555-0188
